title: DEAR JESUS, PLEASE DON'T LET GO OF MY GRANDCHILD. I'M TRYING TO BE STRONG, BUT MY HEART IS BREAKING. 💔🙏
paragraphs: DEAR JESUS, PLEASE DON'T LET GO OF MY GRANDCHILD. I'M TRYING TO BE STRONG, BUT MY HEART IS BREAKING. 💔🙏
An aching prayer from a grandparent standing between fear and faith, trusting the Savior who welcomed little children, hears our cries, and remains faithful even when tomorrow is uncertain.
There are photographs you take because you want to remember a beautiful moment.
And then there are photographs you never imagined you would have to take.
A little child lying on a hospital bed.
A white hospital gown. A pink blanket. A tiny arm surrounded by medical tubing. An oxygen mask covering a face that should be smiling, laughing, and asking questions about the world.
And somewhere behind that photograph is a grandparent whose heart is quietly breaking.
That grandparent is me.
I have prayed many prayers in my lifetime. Prayers of thanksgiving. Prayers for forgiveness. Prayers for protection over my family.
But there is something different about praying when your grandchild is lying in a hospital bed.
The words do not come as easily.
Sometimes all you can manage is a whisper.
"Lord Jesus, please..."
And then the tears finish the sentence.
I look at my grandchild, and I remember how small those hands once were. I remember the laughter, the ordinary days, the little things I never realized were such extraordinary gifts.
How quickly an ordinary day can become a day you will never forget.
One moment, life feels familiar.
The next, you are watching a machine, listening to medical instructions, waiting for another update, and silently asking God for more time, more strength, more mercy.
You discover that even the strongest person in the family can feel helpless.
Because there are some battles love cannot fight with its own hands.
You can hold a child.
You can comfort a child.
You can stay beside a child through the night.
But you cannot command sickness to leave.
And that is when you remember how desperately you need Jesus.
Lord, I cannot heal my grandchild. But I can bring my grandchild before You.
I keep thinking about the words of Jesus in Mark 10:14:
"Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these." (NIV)
In the original Greek, Jesus says:
Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με
Aphete ta paidia erchesthai pros me.
"Let the little children come to me."
These words were spoken when people were bringing children to Jesus and His disciples tried to stop them.
But Jesus did not consider those children an interruption.
He welcomed them.
He took them in His arms and blessed them.
And today, as I look at my grandchild in that hospital bed, I hold on to what this passage reveals about the heart of my Savior.
Children matter to Jesus.
Their lives matter.
Their suffering is not beneath His concern.
Their weakness does not make them less precious.
And although this passage is not a promise that every sick child will immediately recover, it reminds me that I am bringing my grandchild before a Savior whose compassion is real.
That truth gives me somewhere to place my trembling heart.
Because, Lord, I am afraid.
I am afraid of hearing words I do not want to hear.
Afraid of watching another painful procedure.
Afraid of seeing my grandchild struggle.
Afraid of what tomorrow might bring.
And sometimes I am afraid to admit how afraid I really am.
But Your Word does not tell me that faith means pretending I have no fear.
In Mark 9:24, a father desperate for his suffering child cried out to Jesus:
"I do believe; help me overcome my unbelief!" (NIV)
What an extraordinary confession.
Faith and struggle in the same sentence.
Belief and desperation in the same breath.
And Jesus did not reject that father for bringing Him an imperfect faith.
Today, I understand that father's cry in a way I never wanted to understand.
Lord, I believe. Please help the part of me that is trembling.
I believe You are powerful.
I believe You are compassionate.
I believe You are able to heal.
But I also know that I cannot see everything You see, and I cannot control what happens next.
So I am not coming to You with a demand disguised as a prayer.
I am coming as a grandparent who loves this child more deeply than words can express.
I am asking You for healing.
I am asking You for mercy.
I am asking You for another ordinary day when this hospital bed is only a memory.
Another morning when my grandchild can wake up without these frightening surroundings.
Another opportunity to hear that precious voice.
Another chance to hold that little hand without wondering what the next medical update will say.
Lord Jesus, please hear me.
Please place Your mercy over my grandchild.
Please strengthen this little body.
Ease every breath that feels difficult.
Calm every moment of distress.
Relieve pain and discomfort.
Give rest where there has been exhaustion.
Restore strength where sickness has brought weakness.
And if healing comes slowly, give us the patience to endure the waiting without losing hope.
Guide every doctor who examines my grandchild.
Give wisdom to every nurse.
Help the medical team recognize what needs attention, choose appropriate treatments, and respond quickly when something changes.
Bless the medicines, procedures, and care being provided.
Protect my grandchild from complications.
And give us the wisdom to listen carefully, ask the right questions, and make decisions with love and understanding.
Father, I thank You for the people who have dedicated their lives to caring for the sick.
Their work matters.
Their knowledge matters.
Their compassion matters.
And I pray that through their care, my grandchild will receive the help that is needed.
I remember the prayer of the early church in Acts 4:30:
"Stretch out your hand to heal and perform signs and wonders through the name of your holy servant Jesus." (NIV)
They prayed boldly because they knew the power belonged to God.
So I, too, will pray boldly.
Not because my words can force Your hand.
Not because I have earned a miracle.
Not because I can promise what You have not promised.
But because You invite Your children to bring their needs before You.
Jesus, if it is Your will, please grant my grandchild healing and recovery.
Let this little body grow stronger.
Let breathing become easier.
Let the treatments work.
Let the doctors see encouraging progress.
Let the day come when we hear those beautiful words:
"You can take your grandchild home."
Lord, I long for that day.
I long to see this child playing again.
Laughing again.
Sleeping peacefully without the sounds of hospital equipment nearby.
I long for the ordinary things I once took for granted.
Because sickness has taught me something painful.
Sometimes the blessings we overlook are the very blessings we would give anything to experience one more time.
A peaceful night.
A healthy appetite.
A little smile.
A child's laughter filling the house.
What once seemed small now feels priceless.
And perhaps someone reading this understands.
Perhaps you are a grandmother who has cried silently so your family would not see you falling apart.
Perhaps you are a grandfather who keeps saying, "Everything will be okay," while privately asking God for strength.
Perhaps you are a mother or father sitting beside a hospital bed, trying to remain calm while your mind races through a thousand possibilities.
Or perhaps you have already walked through a hospital season that changed your life forever.
If that is you, I want you to know something.
You do not have to pretend before God.
You do not have to manufacture a smile.
You do not have to hide your tears to prove that you trust Him.
Psalm 34:18 says:
"The LORD is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit." (NIV)
In Hebrew, the opening words are:
קָרוֹב יְהוָה לְנִשְׁבְּרֵי־לֵב
Qarov Adonai lenishberei-lev.
"The LORD is near to the brokenhearted."
The Hebrew expression nishberei-lev speaks of those whose hearts are broken or crushed.
It does not describe people who have everything under control.
It describes people who have reached the limits of their own strength.
People like me, in this moment.
And perhaps people like you.
This verse does not say the brokenhearted will never suffer.
It tells us that God is near to them.
And sometimes, when you cannot understand what God is doing, the truth that He has not abandoned you becomes the anchor that keeps your soul from drifting into despair.
I also remember something even more astonishing.
Jesus Himself wept.
John 11:35 tells us:
"Jesus wept." (NIV)
The original Greek is just two words:
ἐδάκρυσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς
Edakrysen ho Iēsous.
"Jesus wept."
At the tomb of Lazarus, the Son of God did not stand untouched by the sorrow surrounding Him.
He wept.
The One who would call Lazarus out of the tomb entered the grief of those who mourned.
That means I do not pray to a Savior unfamiliar with human sorrow.
I pray to Jesus Christ, who knows what tears are.
Who knows what suffering is.
Who knows what it means to face death.
And who conquered the grave through His own death and resurrection.
That is why the Gospel is more than a promise that every painful circumstance will change exactly when we want it to.
The Gospel is the good news that Jesus Christ died for our sins, was buried, and rose again, as proclaimed in 1 Corinthians 15:3–4.
Through Him, sinners can receive forgiveness.
Through Him, broken people can be reconciled to God.
Through Him, death does not have the final victory over those who belong to Him.
And through Him, even in the darkest valley, we have a hope that suffering cannot permanently destroy.
I do not know exactly how this hospital journey will unfold.
But I know who Jesus is.
And I know that my grandchild is precious to Him.
So tonight, or whenever you are reading this, I ask you to join me in prayer.
Heavenly Father,
I come before You in the mighty and merciful name of Jesus Christ.
You know my grandchild.
You know every detail of this little life, every need, every struggle, every fear, and every medical concern.
Nothing is hidden from You.
Father, please look upon my grandchild with compassion.
Bring healing where there is illness.
Bring strength where there is weakness.
Bring comfort where there is pain.
Bring peace where there is fear.
Protect this child through every treatment and every difficult hour.
Let the medical care be effective.
Let the body respond well.
Let each new day bring signs of recovery.
And Father, please watch over the heart of this child.
When the hospital feels frightening, bring reassurance.
When sleep is difficult, grant rest.
When pain comes, bring relief.
When familiar faces are needed, surround this child with love.
Lord, strengthen the parents and the entire family.
You know the exhaustion that cannot be explained.
The financial worries.
The unanswered questions.
The moments when everyone tries to be brave for everyone else.
Provide what is needed.
Send people who will help in practical ways.
Give us unity, patience, courage, and wisdom.
Keep us from blaming ourselves or one another when fear becomes overwhelming.
Teach us to carry each other's burdens.
And Lord, I pray for the grandparents who are watching their grandchildren suffer.
Some are sitting in hospital corridors.
Some are far away and unable to visit.
Some are praying beside a bed.
Some are waiting for a telephone call.
Some are carrying grief they cannot put into words.
Please draw near to them.
Remind them that their tears are seen.
Their prayers are heard.
Their love matters.
And their weakness does not disqualify them from coming to You.
Father, I surrender what I cannot control.
But surrender does not mean I have stopped asking.
I am still asking for healing.
Still asking for recovery.
Still asking for more years, more birthdays, more laughter, more memories.
Still asking to see my grandchild grow.
Yet above all, I ask that Your presence sustain us and Your grace keep us close to Jesus, whatever tomorrow holds.
Please do not let this suffering harden our hearts.
Let it deepen our compassion.
Teach us to treasure life.
Teach us to love more faithfully.
Teach us to pray more sincerely.
And draw our family nearer to the Savior who gave His life to redeem us.
In the precious name of Jesus Christ, our Lord and Savior.
Amen.
There is one more thing I want to say.
I know this world is full of painful stories.
Children fighting illnesses.
Parents exhausted by hospital bills.
Grandparents trying to be strong.
Families praying for miracles.
And sometimes, after seeing so much suffering, people begin to wonder whether God still cares.
I understand the question.
But I cannot look at the cross of Jesus Christ and conclude that God is indifferent to human suffering.
At Calvary, Jesus entered the deepest reality of our broken world.
He bore our sins.
He suffered.
He died.
And on the third day, He rose again.
The cross does not mean every hospital story ends the way we desperately want it to.
But it means God's love has been revealed in Jesus Christ, and His resurrection gives us a hope greater than the grave.
This is the heart of our message at Gospel Warrior.
The scandal of sin brought separation from God.
The grace of Christ offers forgiveness, reconciliation, and new life to everyone who turns to Him in repentance and faith.
And although the Gospel does not promise a life without sickness, it assures believers that suffering cannot cancel the saving work of Jesus.
Romans 8:38–39 reminds us that neither death nor life, nor anything else in all creation, can separate God's people from His love in Christ Jesus.
That is the truth I am holding on to beside this hospital bed.
And that is the truth I want my grandchild to grow up knowing.
If this prayer touched something deep within you, please do not walk away silently.
I want the comments to become more than words beneath a post.
I want them to become a place where people encourage one another, where families discover they are not praying alone, and where believers remember that we are called to bear one another's burdens.
Not to demand a response.
But to remind them that someone cares.
Save this prayer for the difficult nights.
For the moments when medical updates are delayed.
For the mornings when courage feels hard to find.
I also want to invite you to help us continue this Gospel mission.
Gospel Warrior exists to share the truth of Jesus Christ with people who are hurting, searching, struggling, and longing to grow in faith.
Keeping these resources available, producing more Christ-centered teaching, and reaching more families requires ongoing support.
Scripture teaches in 2 Corinthians 9:7 that giving should come from the heart, not from reluctance or compulsion, because God loves a cheerful giver.
That is the spirit in which I invite you.
Not from guilt.
Not from fear.
But because, if you believe in this mission, your willing support can help us continue and expand it.
And please remember: you do not have to purchase anything to receive the grace of God. Salvation is God's gift through Jesus Christ, not something money can buy (Ephesians 2:8–9).
It is that people will come to know Jesus.
That wounded hearts will find hope in Him.
That sinners will repent and receive His forgiveness.
That struggling believers will return to His Word.
And that our families, even through suffering, will discover how precious His presence truly is.
As for me, I am still here.
Still praying.
Still trusting.
Still watching over my grandchild.
Still hoping for the day when this little one can leave the hospital and return home.
And if you remember only one thing from everything I have written, please remember this:
My grandchild may be lying in a hospital bed, but my hope is resting in the hands of the risen Jesus.
